purpose: Find roads or locations that remain degraded or repeatedly deteriorate while excluding unsupported gaps in uploaded history.

execution_tiers.name: Internal-reference persistence
required_data: positive speed, travel time or confirmed positive metric
execution_tiers.claim: Time-weighted recurrence relative to an explicitly disclosed internal reference window

execution_tiers.name: Event-labelled persistence
required_data: independently confirmed baseline or event labels
execution_tiers.claim: Time-weighted recurrence against the uploaded and independently defined reference

mathematical_formulation.persistence: valid observed duration above the disclosed threshold divided by total valid observed duration
mathematical_formulation.gap_rule: Intervals longer than 1.5 times the confirmed sampling interval receive zero duration weight

primary_sources.citation: Bruneau, M. et al. (2003). A framework to quantitatively assess and enhance the seismic resilience of communities. Earthquake Spectra, 19(4), 733-752.
primary_sources.relationship: Supports explicit time-dependent performance loss and recovery measurement. The platform applies a descriptive persistence statistic to uploaded transport histories.

verification_contract: Only finite positive reference and observed values enter relative degradation
Timestamps are sorted deterministically per entity
Long unsupported gaps contribute no duration weight
Repeated inputs return identical persistence and ordering
known_limitations: The default earliest-15-percent reference is an internal comparison window, not automatically a pre-disaster baseline
The result is descriptive and does not attribute deterioration to a hazard
Irregular or sparse observations can reduce the valid weighted duration and are reported
